focus: Git 2.50.1's fsmonitor daemon lifecycle, and why a wedged daemon never recovers
noveltyJustification: Eleven of twelve findings are new to the packet: the man-page lifecycle, the ipcthreads default, the no-op Darwin health thread, the source-admitted infinite cookie wait and the unbounded client read were all unrecorded.

graphEvents.label: Documented fsmonitor daemon lifecycle on macOS
No idle shutdown or self-exit is documented or implemented
The Darwin health thread is an empty stub
The daemon cookie handshake is an acknowledged infinite wait
The IPC client reply read has no deadline

label: The 2.50.1 manual documents only start, run, stop and status over a single working directory, and specifies no idle timeout, lifetime bound, self-exit or TTL.
--ipc-threads=8 is git's compiled default for fsmonitor.ipcthreads, not repo configuration; this checkout sets no fsmonitor.* key.
fsmonitor.starttimeout (default 60 s) is the only lifecycle timeout and bounds startup only, never a request.
On macOS the health thread is a no-op: fsm_health__ctor, fsm_health__loop and fsm_health__stop_async return immediately, so the daemon never monitors or retires itself.
git fsmonitor--daemon stop sends quit and then polls fsmonitor_ipc__get_state every 50 ms with no deadline, so a wedged daemon makes stop hang as well.

Every non-quit query creates a cookie file inside the watched tree and then waits in an unbounded pthread_cond_wait; the source comment calls it an infinite wait and says the timed variant was not implemented.

ipc_client_send_command_to_connection reads the reply with read_packetized_to_strbuf and no poll or timeout, so only EOF or a read error releases the client; this is the exact frame in the packet's sample.
The hang is not a two-owner lock deadlock but an unbounded wait on both sides of the socket, reachable whenever the cookie's filesystem event never reaches the daemon listener.

Event overload is the trigger rather than the defect: a roughly 570k-file checkout plus roughly 2M files under .worktrees with 93 node_modules trees can lose or coalesce the cookie event, and the unbounded wait converts that into a 30-minute hang.
The 2.51, 2.52 and 2.53 release notes contain zero fsmonitor entries, so no announced upstream fix addresses the unbounded cookie wait.
Since no idle exit or health exit exists, PID 17228's disappearance at 09:17:59 indicates a signal or crash rather than a timeout, with the unified log or DiagnosticReports as the resolving check.
Each blocked client holds one of the 8 IPC workers, so a saturated pool also stops answering status and stop, which is why the whole checkout appears frozen.

reason: 8 is the compiled default of fsmonitor.ipcthreads and the repo sets no fsmonitor key.
